# Quint mapping

Each lifecycle edge has `meta.action` and a successful `meta.witness`: source model, trace sequence, step and nondeterministic picks. Journeys retain seed 42, sample index and ITF SHA-256. Quint 0.33.0 accepted 24 traces of up to 100 steps for each of 42 context-local mutable models. This proves each retained witness is allowed; it does not prove exhaustive reachability, invariants or the validity of arbitrary stitched paths through a merged projection. All such projections remain assumed unless independent sources agree on the visible outcome.

The opening state precedes model initialization. Its condition event maps to `init`; every other edge names the actual action reported by Quint MBT metadata, including observable underscore-prefixed world events. Self-loops preserve an observable state; they never count numbered retries. A predicate table records the sampled equivalence class. Omitted values and parameter cases require owner review.

The system membership, notification and identity interpretation machines were also simulated with the same 24-by-100 budget. They strengthen review evidence but are not substitutes for context-owned lifecycle approval. The feedback draft and reproduction recording lifecycles are derived from code and have no Quint model; they remain assumed candidates.

## Whole-product composite actions

`system-actions.qnt` composes the same outcomes rather than owning another user-visible aggregate. Its actions are mapped to the existing outcome owners below; atomic composition and boundary assumptions remain cross-context constraints, not another copied lifecycle.

| Composite actions | Outcome owner / charts | Disposition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| signIn, register, startLink, finishLink, unlinkMethod, automaticLink, forgetSession, proveAgain | Auth outside-account-sign-in; Identity account-sign-in / account-privacy | Existing account and proof outcomes; exact composite parameter equivalence classes need execution binding. |
| confirmDeletion, eraseAccount, requestExport, exportReady, exportFailure, downloadExport | Identity account-privacy | Withdrawal, export and retention outcomes; no new Whole product entity. |
| providerChange, latePayment, refundConfirmed, cancellationConfirmed, advanceTime, timePasses | Billing membership-and-checkout, membership-lifecycle and paid-access | Provider, refund, grace and cancellation variants are visible projections; composition remains a shared invariant. |
| deliverInbox, retireInbox, interactInbox | Friends inbox-notice | Recipient preference, duplicate delivery and source retirement projections. |
| matchPeople, finishMatch | Matchmaking matching; Chess multiplayer / custom-game | Complete match and terminal game outcomes; pairing internals stay upstream. |
| cachePuzzles, captureBoardOutcome, recordBoardOutcome, roomMove | Chess puzzle-attempt, puzzle-result-recovery, multiplayer / custom-game | Visible board and first-result projections; cached-pool bookkeeping is below the UI. |
| loseBoardNotification, failAttempt | Chess result recovery and visible refusal outcomes | Delivery fault itself is below the UI; durable result or explanation remains visible. |
| uploadAt, upload, tryUpload, acknowledge, requestSnapshot, receiveSnapshot, applyPush, optimisticPeerPush, dropReply | Sync engine note-replication and App recovery | Delivery mechanics are below the UI; intended writing, refusals and restored views are projected. |
| disconnect, reconnect, crash, restart, revoke | App opening/update/recovery and the affected owning lifecycle | Recovery must preserve intended effects and end revoked access; no shared transport chart invents a context. |
| init, move, emit | Product map and owning transitions | Initialization, composition and published fact transport; no independent screen state. |

`boundary-assumptions`, `fair-recovery`, `recovery`, `identity-machine` and other system helper/interpretation modules constrain these mappings. Their technical orchestration actions are excluded as separate screen events. This table records ownership and exclusion, not a claim that all composite guards have a one-to-one transition witness or that the whole-product model has been exhaustively checked.
